newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes firmer vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes firmer vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed slightly up against the dollar on speculation that the Central Bank was keen to keep rates low, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.20 to the U.S. currency after opening at 57.23. It closed at 57.20 on Tuesday.
The local currency gained steadily in the morning to a 57.12/14 range on speculation that the central bank would not let it depreciate in the near term, dealers said.
"Aggressive buying in the market by a couple of foreign banks jacked up spot rates (later in the day), taking the dollar up to 57.23 at one time," a Commercial Bank dealer said.
The Central Bank pushed the dollar down by one quarter of a local cent, and fixed buying and selling rates at 56.1800 and 57.3150. It also cut the overnight repo rate to 12.25 percent from 12.5.
Overnight call money closed at 12.5 percent.
"The Central Bank's intentions are clear," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said. "It is keen to push overall rates down." --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
